id.description: The author's stable identifier within the producing platform.

Author.description: Who made the claim. A platform-derived record never reads as something an agent said.

harness.description: The harness the agent ran in, e.g. a coding assistant or a hosted runner.

model.description: The model identifier, pinned to a revision where the provider allows.

Actor.description: What produced the record on the author's behalf.

symbol.description: A symbol within the file, e.g. a function or class name.

commit.description: The commit the anchor was resolved against.

Anchor.description: A code symbol pinned to a commit.

MessageCitation.description: A numbered message in a session. Session messages are immutable.

ref.description: A reference to the evidence itself: a probe run, a test result, a message.

EvidenceClass.description:
How much weight a piece of evidence carries. Only proof and rulings may
block or clear a change; testimony and opinion only route work.

EvidenceSource.description: Where a piece of evidence came from. A separate axis from its class.

subject.description: A named concept in the codebase, e.g. `authz.permission-evaluation`.

unit.description: The unit of a `bound` value, e.g. `ms`, `bytes`, `requests/s`.

scope.description:
Where the proposition holds, as `;`-separated `key:value` pairs, e.g.
`env:prod|staging;tenant:t1`. Absent means everywhere.

strength.description:
The holder's declared kind of reliance, not a confidence. `must`: the
holder breaks if the proposition is false. `should`: it degrades. A
contradiction of a `should` premise is reported as suspect rather than as
a conflict. Comparison never reads it.

Proposition.description:
A typed statement about a subject. Premises (what a change relies on) and
effects (what a change alters) share this shape; two propositions with the
same subject and predicate can be compared.

Predicate.description: The dimension a proposition talks about. Each predicate orders its values on a lattice.

Relation.description: How a proposition's value relates to the predicate's lattice.

Citation.description: A pointer to what a claim rests on.

FootprintEntry.description: A path or symbol a change edits, creates or deletes.

pointer.description: A JSON Pointer into the record.

premises.description: What the change relies on, about code it does not own.

declaredEffects.description: Effects the agent expects to cause. Advisory only: effects are derived, never trusted.

Intent.description: What an agent declares before writing code. Each revision is immutable.

Premise.description: A single premise claimed after the intent, e.g. when relying on one more subject.

decision.description: The id of the decision record.

Stance.description: How a change relates to an earlier decision it encountered as precedent.

anchors.description: Code locations the derivation rests on.

declared.description: Whether the change's author had declared this effect.

contradicts.description: A premise or tenet this effect contradicts, by reference.

DerivedEffectBase.description: The fields every derived effect carries.

anchors.description: Code locations the derivation rests on.

declared.description: Whether the change's author had declared this effect.

contradicts.description: A premise or tenet this effect contradicts, by reference.

ExtractedEffect.description: Found by a deterministic extractor: proof.

anchors.description: Code locations the derivation rests on.

declared.description: Whether the change's author had declared this effect.

contradicts.description: A premise or tenet this effect contradicts, by reference.

DecisionModelEffect.description: Answered by a decision model: opinion, always with its probability.

anchors.description: Code locations the derivation rests on.

declared.description: Whether the change's author had declared this effect.

contradicts.description: A premise or tenet this effect contradicts, by reference.

CodeModelEffect.description: Proposed by a code model: opinion.

commit.description: The commit the diff was taken at.

Derivation.description:
What a platform derived from a diff. A derivation interprets a fact, so it
is a claim; each effect carries how it was derived and its evidence class.

NonEmptyCitations.description: A citation list that must not be empty: decisions and verdicts cite what they rest on.

change.description: The change this claim is about: a Change-Id that survives rebases.

session.description: The session the claim was made in.

base.description: The base commit the claim was made against.

seq.description: Position within the session, when the record came from one.

supersedes.description: The id of a record this one replaces.

countersig.description: The platform's Ed25519 signature over the RFC 8785 canonical record, added when the change lands.
